captures.description: A laptop resolves a name and loads a page. Nothing is wrong here.

expect.note: No finding of any kind. A false positive here is a bug.

captures.description: Two lookups, no response in the capture. Suspected, never confirmed.

expect.note: Retried after 5 s, no response seen at this capture point

captures.description: A connection to port 445 answered with a reset.

expect.note: RST/ACK answering the SYN

captures.description: Three connection attempts to port 8080, nothing comes back.

expect.note: Three SYNs, no SYN/ACK and no ICMP. One direction only.

captures.description: A connection attempt answered by an ICMP administratively prohibited.

expect.note: ICMP type 3 code 13 from 192.168.1.1, quoting the SYN

captures.description: Two devices answer ARP for 192.168.1.20 at the same time.

expect.note: Packets truncated at 96 bytes; payload detectors must report themselves as unavailable

captures.description: The interface reports 412 dropped packets, so absence proves nothing.

expect.note: 412 packets dropped by the capture tool; every "no response" in this file is downgraded

captures.description: A device tries to keep an address the server will not give it.

expect.note: NAK answering a REQUEST for 10.14.3.55, server 192.168.1.1

captures.description: Two DHCP DISCOVERs with no offer in the capture.

expect.note: No OFFER at this capture point; a relay or a dead scope would both look like this

captures.description: The connection opens, then the server rejects the handshake with a fatal alert.

expect.note: Fatal alert 48, unknown_ca, for intranet.corp.example. The reset that follows is the same event and must not be reported twice.

captures.description: A 50,000-packet file transfer. Used for the throughput gate.

expect.note: A healthy bulk transfer. No findings; this file is for timing.
